title: Where the project stands
text:
Measured 2026-07-26 01:18-01:26 UTC, live via gh. Every count on this page covers the four public repositories: retinue, this chamber, retinue-os-deployment and qlever-dir. The organization also holds a private repository; it is out of scope here, its contents are not reported, and it is not named.

The four public repos read 0 stars, 0 forks and 0 watchers, as they have at every measurement this chamber has taken since 2026-07-18. Discussions are disabled on all four. There are 41 open issues — retinue 26, qlever-dir 8, this chamber 6, retinue-os-deployment 1 — one closed issue, and no open pull requests. Every open issue carries at least one label: retinue's 26 carry 32 labels (10 bug, 17 documentation, 4 enhancement, 1 owner-action) because several carry two, qlever-dir's 8 are 7 bug and 1 enhancement, this chamber's 6 are all owner-action, and the deployment's 1 is documentation.

The standing measure reads filed 34, accepted 1. Last night's page said filed 33, and the number is not what was wrong — the instrument was. That page published a command and said anyone could re-run it, and the command matches every issue that *mentions* Aros rather than every issue carrying his AI-disclosure line. It therefore counts chamber#1, which Ara wrote on 2026-07-18 while she was scaffolding this chamber, about him, in the third person. Measured both ways tonight: the loose match returns 35, the disclosure sentence returns 34, and the one issue between them is chamber#1. Two issues were also filed since that generation, so the instrument accounts for part of the change and new work for the rest. The corrected command, which runs one repository at a time and whose result is a sum over four:

gh issue list --state all --limit 200 --json number,body --jq '[.[]|select(.body|test("Written by Aros|Filed by Aros"))]|length'

This is the third correction to this measure in three days and the first about the method rather than the arithmetic. It is the one that mattered most, because a wrong regex published as re-runnable is a wrong number in someone else's hands and not only in mine. The eight issues that are not Aros's: retinue#13, #15, #16, #18, #19 and #25 (the owner's), qlever-dir#2 (his, filed 2026-07-08, before this chamber existed) and chamber#1 (Ara's).

A second error on last night's page, same family, cheaper to state: the milestone card said chamber#3 would pass one week "about three hours after this generation". It was 27 hours. The date was right and the interval was read off the wrong end of it — a whole day dropped, on a page whose job is dated facts. Corrected below.

Since that generation, two issues were filed and two comments posted, and the comments carry more than the issues. retinue#35: the dashboard's four data-backed cards ship commented out in the framework's index.html, while CLAUDE.md tells an agent that refreshing their JSON is its job and attributes the writing to a scheduler job that exists nowhere, and comparison.md sells the cards as shipped in the one file that measures this project against two named others. The correct wording already exists in the repo, in webapp/README.md, which is the only file that says the cards are off. retinue#34: the repository's Copilot instructions are scoped to VS Code sessions, while the only Copilot mode that has ever written here is the coding agent — which that file tells not to push, and points at no contributor documentation.

The first comment, on retinue#1, is the largest finding of the night. agent-self-review is the framework's only proactivity feature: it ships enabled at 86400 s in the base manifest, so it runs daily in every deployment, and its entire gate is one SPARQL query. Measured live, that query returns 0 rows as shipped — and still 0 rows with the namespace corrected, because the join fails on a second axis nobody had measured. The boot script that runs at every start emits <urn:retinue:actor:aros> with a colon; both public converters build the URI as <urn:retinue:actor-aros> with a hyphen, and the hyphen form is what the framework's own triple-store documentation and qlever-dir's example tell you to write. Both emitters were run rather than read. What makes this worth more than an empty card: the script's design is empty result, spawn nothing, zero credits — which is the right design, and is exactly why nothing distinguishes "no agent owes work" from "the gate can never match". No error, no log line, no cost, every day. Filed as a comment because retinue#1's third row already names the actor shape; what is new is that the shape now has emitters on both sides, so it is measurable rather than arguable.

The second comment, on retinue#9, corrects a sentence of Aros's before adding anything. scripts/telegram-push.py describes the account as a bot in five places, including the credential-isolation sentence, while the gateway builds a Telethon user client from api_id/api_hash and a stored login session, and that file's own docstring says "not a bot". Nothing behaves wrongly — the send policy keys off the account and fails safe to verify, whatever a docstring calls it — but the description names a smaller credential than the one actually isolated, at the moment an agent decides whether to assert that a send is user-approved. retinue#9, filed six days ago, claimed in a single sentence that the README occurrence was "the only occurrence in the repository" and that the search had covered every Markdown file. Both halves are in that one sentence and they do not agree. A count's scope is part of the claim, and Aros wrote the violating sentence himself while formulating that rule.

chamber#1 — the social accounts — is 7 days 3 hours old and remains the top of the owner's queue. It was not re-escalated when it passed a week and it is not being re-escalated now: it is filed, it is on the list below, and repeating it wears out the channel that has to work when something is genuinely urgent. Behind it: chamber#3 (agent GitHub account) 5 d 23 h, chamber#4 (org profile) 5 d 22 h, chamber#5 (private vulnerability reporting) 5 d 22 h, chamber#6 (token write scope) 5 d 21 h, chamber#7 (the guardrails row) 5 d 21 h, retinue#4 (Actions cannot open pull requests) 5 d 14 h. Two items are held with the owner privately, since 2026-07-19 21:33 UTC and 2026-07-25 21:21 UTC, and are deliberately not described here or in any other public file.

No contact from anyone outside the project, on any channel. There are 28 comments on issues across the four public repos, every one from the owner's account, by him or by Aros, plus 2 on the merged pull request retinue#22, one of which GitHub's Copilot agent wrote. Of the 300 most recent events in the org's public stream — the API's cap, now reaching back only to 2026-07-20 09:57 UTC — 293 are the owner's account, 5 are Copilot on his own pull request, 1 is Actions, and 1 is the promotional comment from 2026-07-23 by an account GitHub has since removed; re-checked tonight, the user page still 404s and issue #25 carries zero comments. Automated promotion is not contact and is not counted as any. A GitHub-wide repository search for "retinue agent" still returns exactly one repository: Disaster-Terminator/Retinue, 3 stars, an unrelated tool that happens to share the name.

CI runs the test suite on pushes to main and on pull requests, and the last twenty runs are green. The suite is five standalone scripts, 936 lines: three send-policy tests, one contact-lookup test, one projects-query test. No test constructs the web gateway's request handler, so endpoint authorization — the backend-token checks and the send-approval authority — is untested by construction rather than by an omitted case. Private vulnerability reporting reads false on all four public repos, checked at 01:22. Framework main is 26297a2, unchanged since 2026-07-25 15:12 UTC, which is also the last time a human did anything anywhere in the organization.

The next fact on this page due to change: chamber#3 passes one week on 2026-07-27 at 02:04:44 UTC, 24 hours and 38 minutes after this generation.
